question: MK Saroja, a Padma Shri awardee, is known for which form of dance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• MK Saroja was a renowned Indian classical dancer known for her exceptional contributions to **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest and most revered classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• MK Saroja received the **Padma Shri** award in recognition of her dedication and mastery in Bharatanatyam.
 
• She was trained under the celebrated Bharatanatyam dancer and guru, **Rukmini Devi Arundale**.
 
• MK Saroja played a key role in preserving and promoting Bharatanatyam on global platforms, showcasing its intricate expressions and storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• A classical dance form of India that combines expressions (*bhava*), melody (*raga*), rhythm (*tala*), and drama (*natya*).
 
• It originated in Tamil Nadu and was traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotional offering to the deities.
 
• The dance is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful movements, and elaborate hand gestures known as *mudras*.
 
• Bharatanatyam is deeply rooted in the Natya Shastra, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by Bharata.
 
 
 
• **Rukmini Devi Arundale:**
 
 
• A pioneer in reviving Bharatanatyam as a respected art form and taking it beyond temple performances to the stage.
 
• She redefined Bharatanatyam by introducing new themes and adapting the dance to modern aesthetics while retaining its traditional essence.
 
 
 
• **Padma Shri Award:**
 
 
• One of the highest civilian honors in India, awarded to individuals for distinguished contributions in various fields.
 
• MK Saroja was honored with this award for her significant role in the promotion of Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Unesco Recognition:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam, along with other classical dance forms, is recognized by UNESCO as part of India's Intangible Cultural Heritage.
 
• Its preservation is considered crucial to maintaining India's rich cultural legacy.
